$schema: Warehouse picking technology archetypes on a flexibility (F) vs efficiency (E) frontier, from the integration spec of 2026-11-25. Coordinates, sub-scores, constraints and the decision settings are expert-judgement defaults on 0–100 scales, not measured data: calibrate before relying on them. Vendors are examples, not an exhaustive list.

config.$comment: The decision settings. flexibility: inputs → F_required (a → 0, b → 1; a > b inverts). efficiency: inputs → efficiency pressure P. F_target = clamp(F_required − shift × (P − 0.5)). boundary: the recommendation is a boundary case if it changes when F_target moves by ± this much. Costs in EUR.

site_inputs.$comment: The site inputs of the screening form: range, step and wording. Ratios are 0–1 here and shown as % on the page; costs in EUR.

demand_cv_weekly.label: Weekly demand variability
demand_cv_weekly.description: Coefficient of variation of weekly order lines (standard deviation ÷ mean). 0.1 is steady; 0.6 is very volatile.

annual_sku_churn.label: Yearly SKU churn
annual_sku_churn.description: Share of the SKU range replaced in a year.

lease_horizon_years.label: Lease horizon
lease_horizon_years.description: How long the site is committed: lease left, or how long the operation is planned to stay.

peak_to_average_ratio.label: Peak-to-average ratio
peak_to_average_ratio.description: Busiest week (or season) as a multiple of an average week. Not the same as the comparison's peak-hour factor.

growth_uncertainty.label: Growth uncertainty
growth_uncertainty.description: How unsure the volumes a few years out are.

share_skus_outside_container.label: SKUs outside a container
share_skus_outside_container.description: Share of SKUs that don't fit a 600 × 400 × 300 mm tote or bin up to about 30 kg.

flat_floor.label: Floor
flat_floor.description: Mobile shelf robots need a level, smooth slab.

rent_eur_per_m2_year.label: Rent
rent_eur_per_m2_year.description: Rent or equivalent occupancy cost per m² of floor a year.

order_lines_per_day.label: Order lines per day
order_lines_per_day.description: Order lines picked on an average day.

archetypes.name: Fixed AS/RS shuttles
archetypes.mechanism: Aisle-bound shuttles and lifts feed totes to fixed stations
archetypes.weaknesses: Long lead time, high sunk capex, hard to relocate or resize
archetypes.best_fit: Stable, high-volume, owned site, 10+ year horizon

archetypes.name: Cube storage
archetypes.mechanism: Robots on top of a stacked bin grid dig out bins and deliver them to ports
archetypes.strengths: Highest density per m², modular grid
archetypes.weaknesses: Bin size limit, slower deep digs, grid tied to building
archetypes.best_fit: High rent, small-to-medium items, stable mix

archetypes.name: Climbing robots
archetypes.mechanism: Robots climb racks to retrieve totes and drive them to stations
archetypes.strengths: Good density, robots scale with peak
archetypes.best_fit: Mid-volume e-commerce and retail, moderate volatility

archetypes.name: Shelf-to-person (Kiva-type)
archetypes.mechanism: Robots lift mobile shelves and bring them to pick stations
archetypes.strengths: Fast install, flexible item sizes, relayout in software
archetypes.weaknesses: Aisles cost density, needs flat floor
archetypes.best_fit: Volatile SKU mix, 3PL, medium lease horizon

archetypes.name: Collaborative AMRs
archetypes.mechanism: Robots carry totes, pickers walk to fixed shelving
archetypes.strengths: Minimal capex, works in existing racking, subscription pricing
archetypes.weaknesses: Walking remains, lower throughput per picker
archetypes.best_fit: Short contracts, brownfield sites, uncertain growth

archetypes.name: Manual picking
archetypes.mechanism: Pickers walk to static shelving with carts
archetypes.best_fit: Low volume, very volatile, low labour cost
